name: Warp Records
founders: Steve Beckett, Rob Mitchell and Robert Gordon
ownershipStory: Founded in 1989 out of the FON record shop in Sheffield, where Beckett and Mitchell sold imported Chicago house and Detroit techno. Gordon left early. The label stayed independent, moved to London, and Mitchell died in 2001. Beckett has continued to run it.
hook: A Sheffield shop label that sold UK bleep techno, then in 1992 told its buyers this music was for listening at home.
blurb: Warp began in a Sheffield record shop in 1989. Its first records were bleep techno, heavy bass made for clubs, influenced by the Detroit and Chicago records the shop sold. In 1992 it released a compilation called Artificial Intelligence and described it as electronic listening music, for home rather than the dance floor. The sleeve showed a robot relaxing in an armchair next to a Kraftwerk record, and Aphex Twin and Autechre were both on it. That marketing decision became a genre: by telling buyers this was music for the mind as much as the body, Warp set up what journalists and a 1993 internet mailing list soon called intelligent dance music, a name most of the artists disliked and which stuck anyway. It is one of the few UK independent labels of its generation still owned by a founder.
